record.paper_title: Infrared tip-tilt sensing: on-sky experience, lessons learned and unsolved problems
record.original_question: What spot-displacement and loop-control algorithms can make an infrared tip-tilt sensor produce stable, accurate tip-tilt estimates when the adaptive-optics correction gives only a low-Strehl, partially corrected point-spread function, especially for off-axis guide stars where anisoplanatism broadens the spot and a diffraction-limited core can break into multiple time-varying speckles? The algorithm must avoid the increased noise of reading larger detector regions for centroiding and avoid simply tracking the brightest speckle, because that speckle can change with time and yield an inaccurate tip-tilt estimate.

evidence.quote: The second part of the paper deals with unresolved challenges for IR TTS. These include algorithms and loop stability in the low Strehl regime, using IR TTSs to measure higher-order modes and guiding on multiple guide stars with diﬀerent magnitudes.

Matters become complicated at modest Strehl ratios (below 10%), where the core can degenerate into two or more speckles (Fig. 7). The spot on the TTS becomes larger due to anisoplanatism, so a larger detector region is needed. Since reading more pixels increases the read noise on each pixel, and since the error in the centroid measurement increases with number of pixels even if the noise were the same, then it follows that the centroid algorithm will suﬀer from increased noise. However, peak ﬁnding algorithms, such as the correlation algorithm, will track the brightest speckle, which will change with time and lead to an inaccurate tip-tilt estimate. Optimal spot displacement algorithms for this régime are an open research problem.
There are still a number of unsolved research problems and these are listed here: – Measuring centroids from partially corrected PSFs ( e.g., oﬀ-axis stars).

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is identified within the adaptive-optics literature as an unresolved research challenge: optimal spot-displacement algorithms for low-Strehl, partially corrected PSFs in infrared tip-tilt sensing are explicitly listed as open. No published algorithm has been demonstrated to be optimal in this regime; centroiding for partially corrected off-axis PSFs remains an active research topic in extreme/wide-field AO instrumentation development.
